exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 A Plan to Go Hiking
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: Tom, are you free this Saturday? I'm planning to go hiking in the hills.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: That sounds great. I really need some time in nature after a busy week.

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: Me too. They say there are many rare birds in that forest.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Wonderful. Should we bring a camera to take some photos?

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: Yes, but let's be quiet so we don't frighten the animals.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Good idea. And we must take all our rubbish home with us.

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: Of course. We should leave the woods as clean as we find them.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Agreed. Let's meet at the bus stop at eight in the morning.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 Why Bees Matter
exercises.speaker: uk_female
exercises.transcript: Bees are small, but they play a huge part in nature. As they fly from flower to flower, they help plants to make seeds and fruit. Without bees, many plants could not grow, and the animals that eat those plants would lose their food. In this way, these tiny insects help to keep the balance of nature. Sadly, bees are now in danger because of pollution and the loss of wild flowers. We can help them by growing more flowers and by keeping our gardens free of harmful chemicals. Protecting bees means protecting a healthy world for us all.
exercises.translation_cn: 蜜蜂虽小,却在自然中作用巨大。它们在花丛间飞舞,帮助植物结出种子和果实。没有蜜蜂,许多植物无法生长,以这些植物为食的动物也会失去食物。就这样,这些小昆虫维系着自然的平衡。可惜由于污染和野花减少,蜜蜂如今处境危险。我们可以多种花、不在花园里使用有害化学品来帮助它们。保护蜜蜂就是为大家保护一个健康的世界。

options: They would move to the city.

options: Because of pollution and the loss of wild flowers.

questions.stem: What is one way we can help bees?
options: Grow more flowers in our gardens.

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Should We Keep a Wild Bird?
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Look, Mum, I found this little bird in the park. Can we keep it at home?

transcript.speaker: Mum
transcript.text: It's lovely, Ben, but I'm not sure a wild bird should live in a cage.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: But it might be safer with us. Outside, bigger animals could hunt it.

transcript.speaker: Mum
transcript.text: I understand, yet a wild bird belongs in its natural home, where it can fly freely.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: So what should we do? It looks a little weak.

transcript.speaker: Mum
transcript.text: Let's care for it until it is strong, and then set it free.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: That sounds fair. I don't want it to be unhappy in a small cage.

transcript.speaker: Mum
transcript.text: Good boy. Helping an animal back to nature is the kindest thing we can do.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 Everything in the Sea Is Linked
exercises.speaker: uk_female
exercises.transcript: Life in the ocean is closely linked together. Small fish eat tiny sea plants, and bigger fish eat the small fish. Even the largest animals depend on this long chain of life. When people take too many fish from the sea, the whole chain can be broken. Other animals then lose their food and may fall in number too. This shows that the balance of the ocean is easy to harm but hard to repair. By fishing carefully and keeping the water clean, we can help to protect every living thing in the sea, from the smallest plant to the greatest whale.
exercises.translation_cn: 海洋中的生命紧密相连。小鱼吃微小的海洋植物,大鱼吃小鱼,就连最大的动物也依赖这条漫长的生命链。当人们从海里捕捞过多的鱼,整条链条就可能断裂。其他动物随之失去食物,数量也可能下降。这说明海洋的平衡容易被破坏却难以修复。通过谨慎捕鱼、保持水质清洁,我们就能保护海里从最小的植物到最大的鲸鱼的每一个生命。

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 A Visit to the Nature Reserve
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: Welcome to our nature reserve. Here we protect many rare plants and animals.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It's beautiful here. Why was this reserve set up?

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: Years ago, this forest was almost destroyed, and many species nearly disappeared.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: That's sad. So what did people do to save it?

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: We stopped the hunting, cleaned the rivers, and planted thousands of young trees.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: And did the animals come back?

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: Yes, slowly. Restoring nature takes many years, but the balance is returning.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What a wonderful job. I'd love to help with conservation one day.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 A Tip for Nature Lovers
exercises.speaker: uk_female
exercises.transcript: Here is a simple tip for anyone who loves nature. The next time you feel tired or worried, try spending a little time outdoors. Walk in a park, sit by a river, or just watch the clouds in the sky. Studies show that time in nature can lift our mood and have a positive effect on our minds. You do not need to travel far; even a small green space near your home can help. While you are there, look closely and be aware of the beauty around you. A few quiet minutes with nature today can leave you feeling calmer and happier.
exercises.translation_cn: 给所有热爱自然的人一个简单建议:下次当你感到疲惫或烦恼时,试着到户外待一会儿。在公园散步、坐在河边,或只是看看天上的云。研究表明,亲近自然能提升我们的心情,对头脑有积极的影响。你不必走远,哪怕是家附近一小片绿地也能帮上忙。在那里,仔细观察、留意身边的美。今天与自然共度几分钟安静时光,就能让你感到更平静、更快乐。
